name: underscores
label: Mom + Pop
lede: She started posting dubstep at 13, taught herself guitar to make a debut, then wrote her best-reviewed record on escalators and in airports. underscores now opens arenas for Charli XCX.

eras.title: Dubstep at thirteen
eras.text: A San Francisco kid with a Grammy-nominated father's studio gear and a Skrillex habit put out one-offs on SoundCloud for years. Then she started singing on her own records, and the EPs are where the voice shows up.

years.h: A thirteen-year-old in San Francisco uploads dubstep to SoundCloud
years.p: [[underscores|ab1a3f85-e0ea-470a-af5c-175447ae774c]] works from her father's computers, chasing the sound design she hears in Skrillex. In 2016 she places second in the Monstercat Mix Contest.
years.xp:
Her father, Ryan Downe, is an audio engineer, and the FADER quotes her on growing up with "computers and instruments just around the house." She was making beat loops in GarageBand at six, and Madonna's 2000 album Music was an early favorite.

Wikipedia has her releasing dubstep and one-offs for years, among them the 2015 single "Mild Season", before she got bored of the sound-design loop and widened her palette.

years.h: She sings on her own record for the first time
years.p: Skin Purifying Treatment is a jazz and EDM hybrid. Per Wikipedia it largely works through questions about gender, and she has said being trans was all she could think about in high school.
years.xp:
Two more EPs followed: We Never Got Strawberry Cake (2019), with a cover she designed herself and calls her proudest work, and Character Development! (2020). Jazz and future bass sit next to the songwriting.

In 2020 she also started a YouTube channel, 2ndgenbias, that analyzed K-pop song structures.

eras.title: Guitar, gecs and a water tower
eras.text: She taught herself enough guitar to make a debut that landed on year-end lists, then spent the fall opening for 100 gecs. By summer she was on the Lollapalooza bill.

years.cap: Fishmonger (2021). Cover photographed in Longport, New Jersey.
years.h: She teaches herself guitar and puts it on every Fishmonger song
years.p: Recorded at her parents' house during the pandemic and self-released March 25, after she ran out of production tricks she cared about.
years.xp:
She was tired of keyboard voicings, so she picked up guitar with almost no experience and made herself use it on every track. Guests included 8485, Gabby Start and Maxwell Young. The cover water tower was shot in Longport, New Jersey, the coastal-town setting behind the concept. Singles were "Second Hand Embarrassment" (February 2) and "Kinko's Field Trip 2006" (March 2).

The Atlantic ranked it fifth on its best albums of 2021, and The Line of Best Fit later named it among the greatest hyperpop albums. A DeadAir Legacy Edition with 24 tracks came out in February 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician) · The FADER: 9 takeaways · underscores cover story
years.h: She opens for 100 gecs, from Oakland to Terminal 5
years.p: The North American run opens October 8 at the Fox Theater in Oakland and closes December 9 at Terminal 5 in New York.
years.xp:
Lido put her in touch with manager Dorothy Caccavale, and Glaive and Blink-182's [[Travis Barker|3aebd566-7ff8-4b29-b017-051b6ec55861]] were already paying attention. The FADER profile calls this the moment she realized her career was blowing up.

She remembers it differently from the inside. After Fishmonger took off she was "really on autopilot, and kind of vacant at the time."

years.src: Wikipedia: Boneyard AKA Fearmonger · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician)
years.h: Blink-182's Travis Barker drums on her second EP
years.p: Boneyard AKA Fearmonger is self-released. Barker plays on "Tongue in Cheek", and Brakence co-produces.
years.xp: She has said she wouldn't open Ableton until she had a song idea, after five months of writing nothing. The Atlantic's Spencer Kornhaber called the EP an improvement over Fishmonger, and The FADER called "Tongue in Cheek" a one-of-a-kind mosh pit.

years.h: Lollapalooza gives her the festival's opening day
years.p: She plays the T-Mobile stage in Grant Park, Chicago, on July 28.

eras.title: Welcome to Wallsocket, Michigan
eras.text: She wrote a whole fictional town, ran an alternate reality game to sell it, and told NME hyperpop was dead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wallsocket · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician) · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.h: She invents a Michigan town, then declares hyperpop dead
years.p: Wallsocket is a concept album on Mom + Pop and Corporate Rockmusic, out September 22. It runs through country, folk and emo, with gun violence, class and religion in the plot.
years.xp:
The rollout came with fake Wallsocket websites and an alternate reality game, modeled on the Halo 2 and Cloverfield campaigns she loved. Singles ran from "Cops and Robbers" on May 3 to "Old Money Bitch" on August 16, with Gabby Start on "Locals (Girls Like Us)". The Hometown Tour started July 13.

"I think hyper-pop is officially dead," she told NME that September. The FADER quotes her tying the album's numb, angry sound to antidepressants: "the anger and depression of not being able to feel anything."

The Atlantic placed it seventh on its year-end list. A Director's Cut with four extra songs followed June 28, 2024.

eras.title: Music for malls
eras.text: She toured with Porter Robinson and Danny Brown, then wrote her most direct record in hotel rooms and on escalators. Charli XCX took her on the road.

years.cap: Underscores in a portrait shoot, March 2025
years.h: Coachella hears "Music" before anyone else does
years.p: The song comes out June 27. She made the instrumental on the Porter Robinson tour and recorded the vocals in Chicago with a mic small enough for a backpack.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she played both Coachella weekends and also aired "Copycats" with Danny Brown. The track is a loose homage to Madonna's song of the same name and a return to the dubstep and future bass she grew up on.

Pitchfork's Kieran Press-Reynolds called it "endearingly askew", littered with little tonal jumps and ornate glitches. Mastering was by Heba Kadry.

years.h: She directs the "Do It" video herself, with Dance Dance Revolution
years.p: The single comes out November 4 with Britpop-leaning synths. A remix with South Korean singer Yves premieres January 22, 2026.

years.src: Wikipedia: U (Underscores album) · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.h: U lands with an 8.6 from Pitchfork and an 89 on Metacritic
years.p: Nine songs in 34 minutes. Pitchfork's Walden Green praises the production detail.
years.xp:
She wrote it on the road and calls it music for malls, airports, hotels and supermarkets, drafting lyrics outside high-end stores and recording voice memos on escalators. She produced, mixed and mastered everything but "Music". The Guardian's Alexis Petridis found it less hair-raising than before, closer to late-90s and early-2000s R&B. The Sydney Morning Herald called it the first pop masterpiece of the post-Brat age.

"This is the least poser-y I've felt going into an album so far," she told The FADER, calling it "a celebration of being able to feel and understand emotions."

years.h: The cover of U is a mall in San Francisco
years.p: Japanese illustrator Ochiai Shohei drew the Stonestown Galleria, where she spent time in high school. She did the design direction, he says, and he was on-site director.
years.xp: Each of her albums is tied to a real place: a New Jersey water tower, a Michigan horseshoe statue, now a mall. Ochiai first turned her down over scheduling, then messaged her on Instagram to say he wanted in. The art has yellow headphones near the middle and workers at a sandwich counter.

years.big: "I don't know what my ceiling is, but it definitely feels like this could be it."
years.src: The FADER: 9 takeaways · underscores cover story
yt: FADER interview: opening for Charli xcx, personas, K-pop
years.h: The FADER cover story asks where this ends
years.p: Grey's answer in the July profile, which also covers the K-pop idol dream and the 2ndgenbias channel. Friend umru calls her once "the quietest, most reserved person."
years.xp:
Asked about the arc of her career, she laughs at her own word choice: "It feels really... cataclysmic."

The profile follows her from the underground toward arenas. It also has her saying she feels understood for the first time: "I was feeling kind of misunderstood before. And now I feel really understood."

years.cap: Underscores live in Los Angeles, April 15, 2026
years.src: Charli XCX announces · Charli XCX Performs Live Debuts · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.h: She gives up headline dates to open every Charli XCX show
years.p: Charli's announcement of the Music, Fashion, Film Tour puts underscores on every night. She drops her own headline shows to do it.
years.xp:
The FADER reports she cancelled the back half of her GALLERIA shows, and that she will be playing arenas.

On July 10 she joined Charli at Music Hall of Williamsburg, a 650-capacity pop-up in Brooklyn, to sing "Music" as a duet. Clairo and Kim Petras also came out.

yt: Music, Fashion, Film Tour with underscores, Philadelphia
years.h: Charli XCX opens the tour in Philadelphia and calls her back out
years.p: At Xfinity Mobile Arena on September 11, Charli brings her up for "Do It", a song from U.
years.xp: Stereogum reported the night also had the live debut of Charli's "Persona" and her first "Stay Away" in four years.
